title: Loan Accounting Definition: Principal Basis of a Total-Loss Share, Equipment & Vehicle Loans
content:
**Definition.** The principal an Equipment & Vehicle Loans total-loss share is figured on depends on how the loan stands on the release date: when more than 90 days have passed since the most recent installment due date, the share is figured on the principal balance plus the interest accrued on it from the day after that due date through the release date at the contract rate on an actual/365 basis, that interest rounded to cents; when 90 days or fewer have passed and billed interest remains unpaid, the share is figured on the principal balance plus that billed interest not yet paid; otherwise it is figured on the principal balance.

## Terms used

- **Most recent installment due date** — the due date of the latest installment bill on the loan.
- **Interest accrued** — the principal balance multiplied by the contract rate, divided by 100, multiplied by the days from the day after that due date through the release date, and divided by 365, rounded to cents.
- **Billed interest not yet paid** — interest billed with the loan's installments less interest payments applied, with any interest payment the member's bank returned added back.

## Principal basis by position

| Days from the most recent installment due date to the release date | Billed interest unpaid | Principal the share is figured on |
|---|---|---|
| more than 90 | any | principal balance plus interest accrued since the day after that due date |
| 90 or fewer | some | principal balance plus billed interest not yet paid |
| 90 or fewer | none | principal balance |

## Hypothetical worked figures

- Principal 100000.00 at a contract rate of 7.3, release 100 days after the most recent due date: interest accrued is 100000.00 multiplied by 7.3, divided by 100, multiplied by 100 and divided by 365, that is 2000.00; the share is figured on 102000.00.
- Release 90 days after the most recent due date with 1250.00 of billed interest unpaid: the share is figured on the principal plus 1250.00.
- Release 40 days after, nothing unpaid: the share is figured on the principal balance alone.
